learning.why: teacher just showed with the gaay example that one thing gets only one mark, and asked directly about one gaay, so now I know it's always one
Teacher connected leftover marks to mistakes: adding an extra mark or marking a cow twice

end.summary:
Practised making one mark for each object.
Matched marks to objects to identify missing or extra objects.
Used the example of stones for boats: remove one stone when each boat returns.
Sometimes tied two marks to one object or left an object unmarked; this was not consistently corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Parth practised keeping track by making one mark or placing one stone for each object, then removing or crossing one for each return. They explained correctly that no stones left means all boats returned, and that one remaining mark means one cow is still away. They still sometimes mixed up whether an extra mark meant a repeated mark or an object still outside, so this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, try matching small groups of toys with one token per toy, checking each toy once.
